title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Handling Client Property
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: Upon the termination of a retainer, a client requests their original file documents back. The client still owes the paralegal $500 in unpaid legal fees. What right does the paralegal possess regarding the client's documents?
options: The right of absolute ownership over all original documents.
The right to destroy the documents until the fee is paid.

A solicitor's lien (possessory lien), which allows the paralegal to hold onto the client's property until the fees are paid, provided doing so does not materially prejudice the client's legal position.
A mechanic's lien, which allows the paralegal to auction off the documents.
questions.explain: A legal practitioner in Ontario has the common law right to assert a retaining lien (solicitor's lien) over a client's papers and property in their possession to secure payment of costs. However, under the Rules of Conduct, this lien must not be asserted if it would materially prejudice the client's position in an ongoing proceeding.
